name: Commune — Shared Dreaming & Memory Circle Network
description: Commune facilitates structured BCI-linked group dream sessions for 4–12 participants, hosted in licensed sleep-spaces equipped with synchronized neural induction hardware. Participants enter a shared semi-lucid dream environment seeded by a facilitator's 'landscape memory' — a deeply held personal space donated as the session's architecture. Within this space, participants can share curated memory fragments, engage in collaborative symbolic processing, or simply rest inside a consciousness larger than their own. The practice draws from pre-Collapse group therapy, Indigenous collective ritual traditions, and experimental neuroscience.
story_hooks: A character joins a Commune grief circle for a lost friend and discovers, inside the shared dream, that the 'landscape' being used as architecture belongs to someone who claims no connection to the group.
A facilitator's donated landscape begins changing between sessions without their input — and the changes seem to be responding to what participants said in previous circles.
A Commune network across three districts appears to be spontaneously synchronizing, with participants in separate sessions reporting identical dream events on the same nights.
